content:
When trying to build the doc for a course (it basically contains Mathlib+5/6 files, so my goal is to offer students the doc for the fixed commit I picked), I get a message from github telling me that some file exceeds the 100MB limit:
https://github.com/faenuccio-teaching/Beijing_Jun26/actions/runs/26359941541/job/77593450884#step:5:13824

Is this a known problem, and is there a workaround? Or am I doing something wrong?
Is it the bmp file that maps identifier names to urls in the doc?
remote: error: File docbuild/.lake/build/api-docs.db is 118.46 MB
Probably not (not sure, honestly...)

Are you intentionally not gitignoreing the .lake folder?
Using LFS (as the error recommends) is fine, although it might require checking some checkbox when students install Git for them to be able to check it out.
There are too many :check: in your sentence for me to parse it properly... :rofl: That being said, no: I'm not not gitignoring it on purpose, so let me try.
What's a LFS, btw?

It's an acronym for "large file storage", it basically means that git will just upload the file to somewhere and then GitHub only needs to keep a link to it. But it's designed to work mostly seamlessly with git
Well, but at any rate my students won't ever need to do anything git-ish with the doc, just access it online, no? So where should the problem come from?

If all you want is to host the docs, why are you committing the build to git?
As in, did you write this code, and if so why? https://github.com/faenuccio-teaching/Beijing_Jun26/blob/c625d7d982e55dc5315f1c388bbcbcb90d59774c/.github/workflows/docgen-action.yml#L35-L49
No, actually @Anne Baanen wrote it for me for a previous course (where it worked fine) and now I seem to have this problem with the file size
At any rate, the point, I guess, is that I want to deploy the doc as a webpage hosted in that repo, so I believe that committing the build is necessary.

They for sure know a ton more about this than I do, so now I'm not sure anymore.
But my understanding is (based on docgen-action's README) is that you should just enable GH Pages in your repo's settings and it should deploy automatically.
This is what happened last time, and they suggested to simply copy the yml from the previous course. There must be something tricky going on about this size issue.
It's not a huge problem at any rate, I was just wondering whether I was the first to encounter it.

Snir Broshi said:

Are you intentionally not gitignoreing the .lake folder?
Using LFS (as the error recommends) is fine, although it might require checking some checkbox when students install Git for them to be able to check it out.

OK, gitignoring .lake turned out to be the solution, thanks!

EDIT No, that's not true. I am now in a limbo where

  • when I push, my home-page is built and deployed, but the .../docsis empty;
  • If I run the action building the docs, the homepage github.io is empty but ..github.io/docs contains the documentation
  • if I now run the action deploying the site, I can get back the homepage but the docs vanishes again.

It looks like Heisenberg is around... :atom:
Any clue @Anne Baanen ?

Ooh, this is the new backend database that docgen uses to store information while compiling, no idea it would be so big. I think this database is different from the .bmp used by the actual site for searching (but this could change).

The right solution is to only add docbuild/.lake/build/doc to your repo (rather than the whole of docbuild), since that contains the HTML output files. Let me try and make a fix.
Do you actually want to offer the students html files in a git repo, or is a url they can visit which has the right doc version sufficient?

Eric Wieser said:

Do you actually want to offer the students html files in a git repo, or is a url they can visit which has the right doc version sufficient?

The goal last time, as I remember it, is that the API docs stay constant while changes are being made to the code and to other pages. Which would require a setup like this. But just to confirm, @Filippo A. E. Nuccio, is this still the case?
Yes, it is!
Okay!
(as a matter of fact, Mathlib will probably not be updated, but other files in the project will)
I don't understand why that constraint means that you need to check in the .lake folder vs letting github rebuild the doc-gen outputs and cache them
What I want to avoid is that on every push the doc is regenerated. It takes a lot of time and is perfectly useless since I am never changing mathlib.
Ah, that is slightly different from what I understood. I thought you absolutely didn't want changes to show up, rather than preferring not to waste time on probably unnecessary rebuilds.
Ah

Well, there won't be any change to mathlib so I think that the two are equivalent. So if one makes your life easier I'm happy with whatever is best for you. My problem was the long time I had to wait to get an update of the site each time I push
I should have a fix, could you give me push access please? :blush:
Done

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Well, there won't be any change to mathlib so I think that the two are equivalent. So if one makes your life easier I'm happy with whatever is best for you. My problem was the long time I had to wait to get an update of the site each time I push

Mhm, it really just means we should treat the goal as fixing a bug of docgen(-action) where caching is broken. Rather than a feature that is not officially supported.
Yes, and I'm sorry if I derailed in some #xy

Anne Baanen said:

Mhm, it really just means we should treat the goal as fixing a bug of docgen(-action) where caching is broken.

I think it's fixed, see the last comment of https://github.com/leanprover-community/docgen-action/issues/28
